title: Automated Data-Controls Request Diagnostic, Risk-Scoring, and SLA Commit Map
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Problem statement:
Customers (enterprise and mid-market) submit varied non-bug requests that touch logging, retention, PII handling, and audit exports. Current triage is manual, inconsistent across SEs and CSMs, and lacks measurable SLAs. That leads to unpredictable lead times, missed security gating, and poor downstream estimations for Eng/Infra.

Goal:
Design and ship an intake + auto-classification flow that: 1) collects consistent diagnostic signals from customers, 2) produces a reproducible risk score and routing recommendation, 3) surfaces an SLA commit to customers and internal stakeholders, and 4) provides templated response artifacts for the frontline (SE/CSM/Support).

Core deliverables:
- A one-page Diagnostic Questionnaire (web form and PDF) optimized for enterprise legal/compliance triggers (retention windows, data residency, audit frequency, export scope).
- Auto-classification rules: deterministic heuristics + ML-backed tagger to assign request type (redaction, retention change, export, PII inquiry), estimated effort bucket, and security flag.
- Risk-Score algorithm: combines sensitivity (PII/PHI), scope (number of orgs/projects), and requested change surface (runtime logging change vs historic export). Outputs: low/medium/high and recommended SLA band.
- SLA Commit Map: standard response & resolution SLOs by risk band (e.g., initial reply 48h for medium, 4h for high; resolution windows and escalation path).
- Templated customer-facing responses and internal runbook for reviewers.
- Telemetry requirements for measuring intake-to-resolution lead time and accuracy of auto-classification.

Non-goals:
- Building full RBAC policy engine or export tooling. (Those are Eng/Infra deliverables.)

Trade-offs discussed:
- Heuristic-first vs ML-first classification: we will implement deterministic rules for initial GA to ensure explainability for legal reviewers; plan to add ML tagger after 2 cycles and compare precision/recall.
- SLA aggressiveness: tighter SLAs increase operational load. We propose tiered SLAs with automated escalation to on-call for high-risk but allow a formal review step for complex exports.

Acceptance criteria:
- Diagnostic form implemented in Zendesk + internal Confluence form with required fields validated.
- Auto-classification rules implemented as a serverless function (PoC) and documented; initial precision >= 85% on a seeded test set of 120 historical requests.
- SLA Commit Map published in Confluence and wired into support macros/templates.
- Two example customer responses (redaction and audit-export) approved by Legal and Security.
- Telemetry dashboards created in Datadog with intake->first-response and intake->resolution metrics per risk band.

Links to artifacts:
- PRD (internal): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/PM-71111+Data+Controls+Diagnostic+PRD
- Diagnostic form mock (drive): https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1xDiagFormMock
- Support macro templates (Zendesk): https://support.redwood.ai/macros/DC-templates
- Seed dataset for classifier (internal drive): https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1xSeedSet
- Incident learnings (past misses): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Data+Controls+Incidents

Implementation notes for Eng:
- PoC function should return tags [type, risk_band, effort_bucket, require_security_review] as plain text to simplify integration with Zendesk and CRMs.
- Ensure idempotent logging of intake events for telemetry (request_id preserved).
- Encryption-at-rest and access auditing must be enforced for intake payloads containing sample PII.

Rollout plan:
1) Week 0-2: finalize questionnaire + deterministic heuristics + legal signoff on templates.
2) Week 3-4: deploy PoC classification into staging; run the classifier on a shadow stream of incoming requests.
3) Week 5: pilot with 3 SE teams + 2 enterprise customers (invite-only).
4) Week 6-8: iterate on misclassifications, tune thresholds, publish SLA map, and enable macros.

Monitoring & metrics:
- Metric 1: % of intakes auto-classified (goal: >80% within 2 weeks of GA).
- Metric 2: initial reply SLA compliance by risk band (goal: 95% for low/medium; 90% for high during pilot).
- Metric 3: classifier precision on seeded set (goal: >=85%).

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Who owns the 'require_security_review' triage step for high-risk items? (Security or Product Ops?)
- Which support queues should be allowed to override risk band and what is the audit trail?
- Should we surface partial sample payloads to Legal on intake, or require customers to upload sanitized samples?

Next steps / owners:
- PM (Priya): finalize questionnaire and stakeholder review (Legal, Security, Support) — due 2025-02-18.
- Design (Leah Kim): deliver form UI + PDF template — due 2025-02-20.
- Eng (Marcus Alvarez): implement PoC serverless classifier and seed dataset integration — POC ready 2025-03-03.
- Security (Omar Ruiz): define approval gate for 'high' risk — review by 2025-02-25.

acceptance_criteria: Diagnostic form and deterministic rules in staging; classifier PoC with >=85% precision on seeded set; SLA map published and templates approved by Legal and Security; telemetry dashboards tracking intake->first-response and intake->resolution.
notes_for_support: Use support macro 'DC-AUTO-REPLY' for low/medium; escalate to 'DC-HIGH-ESCALATE' macro which opens a SecOps ticket for high-risk. All overrides must include reason and approver initials.
qa_plan: Seeded test set (120 items) for classification precision; end-to-end test of intake -> initial reply macro -> tracked resolution; pilot customers to validate clarity of questionnaire.
out_of_scope: Changes to long-term retention engine, data export tooling, or underlying infra RBAC policies. Those will be separate engineering projects after intake and scoring are stable.
